To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The U‐Th‐Pb isotopic systematics of arc lavas are consistent with a short residence time of the mantle wedge (10–100 kyr), but (2) the isotopic compositions of the mantle wedge are inconsistent with a short residence period of the mantle wedge, which would be expected if the wedge was metasomatized by fluids from the slab.
the U-series disequilibria observed in the samples are best explained by the addition of a sediment melt component that was introduced to the mantle wedge 8–10 kyr ago.

“The timing of fluid delivery from subducting sediments is constrained by the disequilibrium of the U-series isotopes in the mantle fragments, which indicate that the sediments were delivered to the mantle wedge about 10 kyr before fluid delivery.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of subduction zone processes in the generation of arc magmas and the delivery of volatile components to the mantle.
the geochemical and isotopic composition of arc lavas and the role that they play in the global geochemical cycles of volatile elements.
how the Earth’s volatile budget is replenished and modified by subduction and mantle melting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the subduction zone is the most significant source of volatiles to the upper mantle.
the timing of fluid release from the slab is not well understood and is not well constrained by the available data.
the U-series isotopes in arc lavas are consistent with the presence of sediment melts, aqueous fluids and/or melt‐fluid interactions in the source of the lavas 3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new way to constrain mantle metasomatism and that we have demonstrated that the timing of metasomatism can be resolved.
the U-series isotope systematics of the Batan Island mantle fragments indicate that the subduction zone has been active for at least 10 kyr.
we are trying to constrain the timing and processes of fluid and sediment release from subducted sediments and oceanic crust.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mantle wedge is not a passive reservoir for fluids and melts derived from the subductin zone.
the subducted sedimentary component of arc magmas is not a simple mix of the sedimentary component and mantle peridotite, but rather is the result of a complicated process of mixing and metasomatism.

we can constrain the timing of the arrival of sediment and fluids at the base of a subduction zone, and we can constrain the amount of water that has been delivered to the mantle wedge and that may be transported to the base of the mantle.
